keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria starts the row in 960, although the infobox gives 'Established: 951'. The page names no prefectures; the 960 outline is taken as the realm of 951-959 (confidence by the page's one phrase, 'Shanxi').

26,506 km2 (about 34,000 by the gazetteer's cell count), about a sixth of Shanxi province. Unverified: page budget. The Northern Han page gives no area and no prefecture list, only 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi' and 'based in the traditional Shatuo stronghold of Shanxi' (Five Dynasties page); a Taiyuan-centred outline of this size fits 'small' and the shape lies entirely inside Cliopatria's Later Han shape.
26,506 km2, the same outline as 960; unverified: page budget. The page names no loss or gain of land between 951 and 979; the Song campaigns of 968-977 are not on the pages opened.

region.text: the Northern Han realm: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.note: 951: Liu Min founds the Northern Han in Shanxi. 'Liu Min founded the Northern Han Kingdom, sometimes referred to as the Eastern Han, in 951', 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi', after Guo Wei's coup ended the Later Han. He 'immediately restored the traditional relationship with the Khitans' and 'The Northern Han had placed itself under the protection of the Liao'. Month and place of the proclamation are not on the page.

region.text: the Northern Han realm at its end: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.note: 979: the Song take the Northern Han. 'Ended by the Song dynasty: 979'; Emperor Taizong 'decided to embark on a campaign to finally destroy the Northern Han', and 'After a two-month siege of the capital, the emperor of the Northern Han surrendered and the kingdom was incorporated into the Northern Song.' The Taizong page: 'Emperor Taizong personally led the campaign against Northern Han in 979'.

region.text: the Northern Han realm at its end: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

ledger.note: 979: the Northern Han ends, the last of the Ten Kingdoms to fall before the Song reunified China proper (the Five Dynasties page: 'the Northern Han maintained nominal independence until the Song dynasty wrested it from the Khitans in 979').

wars.name: Battle of Gaoping
wars.outcome: Liu Chong was defeated by Chai Rong of the Later Zhou and died soon afterwards; the pages opened give no territorial result.
wars.note: 'In 954, Liu Chong was defeated by Guo's successor Chai Rong in the Battle of Gaoping and died soon afterwards.' Neither the Northern Han page nor the Liu Chong page mentions the Later Zhou campaigns of 959-960 or the Song sieges of 968-977, and neither gives a month for Gaoping.

wars.name: Song conquest of Northern Han

zones.text: the Northern Han realm at its end: 'a small kingdom located in Shanxi'

wars.outcome: Taizong of Song took the capital after a two-month siege and incorporated the kingdom into the Northern Song.
wars.note: The Northern Han page puts the siege 'in June' without a year and the Taizong page has Taizong setting out on the Liao campaign from Taiyuan in May 979; the pages disagree, so no month is recorded for the surrender.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey fixes any Northern Han border; the realm is a small Shanxi core and its edges are approximate. The Liao protection (not territory) is not a drawn border.

notes:
Northern Han (Cliopatria 960-979, 2 identical shapes of 26,506 km2). The state ran 951-979; Cliopatria starts it nine years late, and this dossier adds northern-han_951 (951-959) from the same outline. Both Cliopatria shapes are verdict ok but 'unverified: page budget': no page opened gives an area, a prefecture count or a loss or gain of land.

Page budget: 4 pages opened (one shared); all are thin. Not on any page opened: the month and place of Liu Min's proclamation; the twelve-prefecture extent; the Liao relationship's form ('nephew', tribute: the pages say only 'protection'); the 954-960 Later Zhou and the 968-977 Song campaigns; the month of the surrender in 979 (the Northern Han page puts the siege 'in June', the Taizong page has Taizong setting out from Taiyuan in May 979 for the Liao campaign).

Vassalage: the Northern Han was under Liao protection from 951 ('placed itself under the protection of the Liao'). The vassal events belong to the Suzerain's dossier (vassal_start with counterpart northern-han, 951; vassal_end 979); the liao-dynasty dossier (group ea-05) should carry them; no event is written here because the schema pairs vassal_start/vassal_end on the suzerain side. Mirrors wanted: later-han (split 951), northern-song (gain 979).
